briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Weed Chains Go National While D.C. Hits Pause on Rescheduling
briefs.top: Michigan operators are finding growth paths — JARS is expanding into Arizona, Ann Arbor's Bloom City Club just opened in Ypsilanti, and a gubernatorial candidate is now courting industry cash to kill the 24% wholesale tax. Nationally, Compass Pathways' psilocybin data keeps the psychedelic pipeline hot even as a DEA judge hits pause on marijuana rescheduling pending an Oct. 13 response deadline.

local.text: JARS Cannabis buys its way into Arizona's top spot
local.text_full: JARS Cannabis buys its way into Arizona's top spot — The Michigan-based chain announced a deal to acquire Sonoran Roots and its eight Ponderosa dispensaries, soon making JARS the largest dispensary chain in Arizona.

local.text: Bloom City Club expands footprint with Ypsilanti store
local.text_full: Bloom City Club expands footprint with Ypsilanti store — Ann Arbor's Bloom City Club opened a new Ypsilanti location and is celebrating with cannabis-themed events throughout October.

local.text: Michigan brands roll out boozy-strength Halloween drops
local.text_full: Michigan brands roll out boozy-strength Halloween drops — Armada Cannabis debuted a 50mg THC "Phillip Noir" blood orange-cranberry cider and a 50mg live-rosin cider collab with Apex Solventless for the season.

local.text: Gubernatorial hopeful courts industry cash on tax repeal
local.text_full: Gubernatorial hopeful courts industry cash on tax repeal — Republican U.S. Rep. John James has pledged to repeal the state's 24% wholesale tax after cannabis executives wrote roughly $90,000 in checks backing his campaign.

local.text: Regulators level the field with record $2M fine
local.text_full: Regulators level the field with record $2M fine — The state revoked 20 grower licenses and fined Clare-based GP Holdings (Millie Montana Industries) $2 million after it shipped dirt and mulch labeled as marijuana flower, clearing a bad actor out of an oversupplied market.

national.text: DEA rescheduling hits a speed bump, not a dead end
national.text_full: DEA rescheduling hits a speed bump, not a dead end — A DEA judge stayed the Schedule III hearing to weigh a GAO report, but the government must respond by Oct. 13 and the pause doesn't affect the April order on state medical and FDA-approved products.

national.text: Compass Pathways' psilocybin posts durable 6-month wins
national.text_full: Compass Pathways' psilocybin posts durable 6-month wins — The company's second Phase 3 trial in nearly 600 patients confirmed COMP360's rapid onset and durable response, with the company targeting a Q4 2026 FDA submission.

national.text: MDMA therapy heads back to FDA with new delivery model
national.text_full: MDMA therapy heads back to FDA with new delivery model — An MDMA application is back before the FDA alongside Oregon's published psilocybin-services outcomes data, pushing providers toward scalable dyadic and group treatment formats.

national.text: Major MSOs post strong growth heading into Q4
national.text_full: Major MSOs post strong growth heading into Q4 — Cresco Labs closed a $50 million Pennsylvania acquisition on $173 million Q2 revenue, while Trulieve expanded its Florida dispensary network and began trading on the NYSE with $271 million in Q2 revenue.

national.text: U.S. vape brand Rove plants a flag in Canada
national.text_full: U.S. vape brand Rove plants a flag in Canada — Rove announced its official entry into the Canadian market starting with Ontario, with plans to expand into additional provinces in coming months.
